s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury
salient_findings: Painful bruise on the hand that persisted despite icing and resting
Ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the left hand
Heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on Magnetic Resonance Imaging
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 30s
The bruise appeared a few days after a twisting injury to the hand
The bruise and pain have persisted for 2 years
The patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
Radiography showed soft tissue swelling but was otherwise unremarkable
Magnetic Resonance Imaging showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion
Pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

shortlist.label: Nora lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury

shortlist.label: Fat necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the patient's history of trauma and the presence of mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition on pathology

shortlist.label: Sclerosing lipogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Pathology findings of mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition and lesional cells positive for CD34 are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Subcutaneous pseudotumor
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical and pathological features, including the presence of a subcutaneous mass with mixed inflammatory infiltrate, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Spindle cell lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of spindled cells with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli, as well as the strong positivity for CD34, are consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a painful bruise that persisted for 2 years, mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, and lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli, along with strong positivity for CD34, are consistent with a Nora lesion.

rejected.label: Fat necrosis
rejected.why: Fat necrosis typically presents with a history of trauma and can have similar histological features, but the presence of spindled and epithelioid cells and strong CD34 positivity is more characteristic of a Nora lesion.

rejected.label: Sclerosing lipogranuloma
rejected.why: Sclerosing lipogranuloma is a rare condition that typically presents with a history of exogenous lipid injection, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Subcutaneous pseudotumor
rejected.why: Subcutaneous pseudotumor is a non-specific term that can refer to various conditions, but the specific histological features and immunohistochemical profile in this case are more consistent with a Nora lesion.

rejected.label: Spindle cell lipoma
rejected.why: Spindle cell lipoma is a type of benign tumor that can have similar histological features, but the presence of extensive pigment deposition and the clinical presentation are more characteristic of a Nora lesion.
